original_question: Given a closed immersed submanifold M of Euclidean space, estimate from below the number of generalized n-periodic billiard trajectories, meaning inscribed n-gons with vertices on M that have extremal perimeter, in terms of the topology of M and the immersion.
target_in_paper: Serge Tabachnikov, subsection "Inner and outer periodic orbits on immersed submanifolds": for a closed immersed submanifold M in Euclidean space, the paper asks for a lower estimate on the number of generalized n-periodic billiard trajectories, defined there as inscribed n-gons on M with extremal perimeter, in terms of the topology of M and the immersion. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.12896))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper very closely: it has the correct ambient setting (a closed immersed submanifold M of Euclidean space), the correct object being counted (generalized n-periodic billiard trajectories), the correct definition of those trajectories (inscribed n-gons with vertices on M and extremal perimeter), and the correct goal (a lower bound depending on the topology of M and the immersion). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.12896))
missing_details: The paper treats n as a fixed period parameter built into the phrase "n-periodic"; a stand-alone version should say this explicitly, e.g. "for a fixed integer n at least 2." The nearby context then distinguishes the known case n = 2 from higher periods. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.12896))

To make the dependence on the immersion fully explicit, it is cleaner to write the data as an immersion i: M → R^N, since the requested lower bound is asked to depend not only on the topology of M but also on the specific immersion. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.12896))

The paper does not impose extra hypotheses such as convexity, embeddedness, hypersurface codimension, or genericity; these should not be added in the refined question. It says only "closed immersed submanifold of Euclidean space." ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.12896))

The term "extremal perimeter" is left at exactly that level in the paper; the nearby text does not replace it with a stronger condition such as nondegeneracy or Morse genericity, so the refined version should preserve that scope. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.12896))
The sentence about outer symplectic billiards is a separate analogous question, not an equivalent reformulation of the inner-billiard counting problem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.12896))
refined_question: For a fixed integer n ≥ 2 and a closed immersed submanifold i: M → R^N, estimate from below, in terms of the topology of M and the immersion i, the number of generalized n-periodic billiard trajectories on M, where such a trajectory means an n-gon inscribed in M (all vertices on M) whose perimeter is extremal among inscribed n-gons. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.12896))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper: the draft is already essentially a paraphrase of the exact problem stated in the Serge Tabachnikov subsection on immersed submanifolds. The only real sharpening needed is to make n a fixed parameter and to display the immersion explicitly as part of the input, while avoiding any extra assumptions not present in the paper. The nearby comments on the n = 2 case and on outer symplectic billiards provide context, but they do not change the main target problem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.12896))
